newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bourse, OM merger might not happen - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bourse, OM merger might not happen - paper.

text.p: The planned merger between the Stockholm Stock Exchange and the Swedish futures and derivatives exchange OM Stockholm, part of OM Gruppen, might not take place, daily Finanstidningen said on Thursday.
"It (a merger) is not around the corner," Bengt Ryden, head of the stock exchange, told the newspaper.
"We have to solve quite a few things before anything is decided," he said.

No negotiations are going on at the moment as the bourse and OM are waiting for a proposal from the Finance Minister, due on June 11, about a government investment of 500 million crowns in the financial market.
Furthermore, the government is seeking parliamentary approval to sell its 50 percent stake in central securities depository VPC.
The bourse and OM will not make a formal decision to resume merger negotiations until parliament has decided on these issues, the newspaper said.
Analysts have previously interpreted the two government moves to mean that the government wants VPC to be included in the planned merger.

Bourse shareholders Handelsbanken, Nordbanken and Foreningsbanken have also thrown a spanner into the works by opposing a proposal to merge the bourse and OM into an OM Gruppen subsidiary, the daily said.
"A number of shareholders have questioned how the merger should look like," Ryden was quoted as saying. "You can say that we have become caught in that."
